newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan hackers launch computer virus in isles row.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan hackers launch computer virus in isles row.

text.p: Computer hackers have joined a Taiwanese backlash against Japan's claim to disputed East China Sea isles, infecting parts of the Internet with an anti-Japanese computer virus, Taiwan's state news agency said on Friday.
The agency said the virus, dubbed The Diaoyus, could debut on the Internet's popular World Wide Web on Saturday, flashing patriotic messages on users' screens before destroying data.
Taiwan's Republic of China government and its political rival China claim the uninhabited islands, calling them the Diaoyus. Japan claims them as the Senkakus.
The virus was designed to attack on the fifth and 20th of every month, the agency said. It said it learned of the destructive virus from industry sources. How widespread it would be was unclear.
The Central News Agency said a message would appear on the screens of computers which became infected reading: "The Diaoyus are the territory of the Republic of China."
Next comes: "Don't even think of getting (the Diaoyus), Japanese monsters."
A final send-off says the virus was planted by: "A patriotic teenager from Feng Hsi Junior High School" before wiping out stored information.
The dispute over the cluster of uninhabited rocky outcrops has kindled fiery passions among Chinese communities since a Japanese right-wing group built a lighthouse and planted flags there in July.
Japan has claimed sovereign rights to the islands and refused to acknowledge that the dispute is still open for discussion with China.
Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
